mathematical_changes.after_statement: Assume AC. In a C*-algebra $A$, use $A$ itself if unital and its minimal unitization otherwise to define spectra. mathematical_changes.before_statement: Assume AC. There is a second-countable locally compact group whose unitary dual, with the Fell topology, is not Hausdorff. Explicitly, let $G=\mathbb R_{>0}\ltimes\mathbb R$ be the affine group of the line, with $(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',b+ab')$ and the topology of $\mathbb R_{>0}\times\mathbb R$, and let $\pi$ be the representation on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ given by $(\pi(a,b)\eta)(u)=e^{ibe^u}\eta(u+\log a)$. Then: (1) $\pi$ is a strongly continuous irreducible unitary representation and $\pi\not\simeq1_G$ (it is infinite dimensional); (2) every unitary character $\chi_t(a,b)=a^{it}$ ($t\in\mathbb R$) lies in the Fell closure of the singleton $\{\pi\}$, so in particular the trivial character $1_G=\chi_0$ does; (3) hence the singleton $\{\pi\}$ is not closed and $\widehat G$ is not a Hausdorff space. This is the source's non-type-I example ([BeHV–08, Example F.2.5(iii)], after [Fell–62, §5]); the source also records the full enumeration $\widehat G=\{\chi_t:t\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{\pi\}$, which is not used here.
mathematical_changes.after_statement: Assume AC. There is a second-countable locally compact group whose unitary dual, with the Fell topology, is not Hausdorff. Explicitly, let $G=\mathbb R_{>0}\ltimes\mathbb R$ be the affine group of the line, with $(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',b+ab')$ and the topology of $\mathbb R_{>0}\times\mathbb R$, and let $\pi$ be the representation on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ given by $(\pi(a,b)\eta)(u)=e^{ibe^u}\eta(u+\log a)$. Then: (1) $\pi$ is a strongly continuous irreducible unitary representation and $\pi\not\simeq1_G$ (it is infinite dimensional); (2) every unitary character $\chi_t(a,b)=a^{it}$ ($t\in\mathbb R$) lies in the Fell closure of the singleton $\{\pi\}$, so in particular the trivial character $1_G=\chi_0$ does; (3) hence the singleton $\{\pi\}$ is not closed and $\widehat G$ is not a Hausdorff space. This is a direct local example of non-Hausdorff Fell topology; no classification of the whole unitary dual or claim about type I is required.
